header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:plondon-bm-10793:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.125C.41: 125C.46: qbbt taken as 'coolness' (qbb 'be cool'); zꜣ may be 'protection' or 'son'; the second clause is unclear.
notes.125C.63: Line 66: written m=k wj, literally 'see me'; taken as the summons 'come' that answers the speaker. Line 70: jm.j-hrw=f, 'those who are in his days', i.e. the people of his time; sense uncertain. Line 73: the !! after the word for uraei is an editorial mark of a scribal oddity.
notes.125D.1: Line 4: ḥn!! is marked by the editor as an odd writing; read as ḥnꜥ 'with'. Line 6: šns and ds are a kind of loaf and a kind of jug; wr 'great' is taken with the meat portion.
notes.134.12: The king's name is written Zm.pl,t with the editor's query; possibly Semti (King Den). bz, 'initiation' or 'introduction', is uncertain.

nodes.text: 'You shall not enter over me,' says the floor of this gate, 'unless you have said my name.'
'Ox of Geb' is your name.
'I will not open for you,' says the bolt of this gate, 'unless you say my name.'
'Toe of Iunmutef' is your name.
'I will not open for you, I will not let you enter past me,' says the doorkeeper of this gate, 'unless you say my name.'
'It is the Coolness(?) of Shu' is your name; 'In the Protection of Osiris' is your name.
Say it, then, to the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
Who is he?
It is Thoth, the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
'Here I am,' says Thoth.
'Why have you come?'
'I have come here.'
'What is your condition?'
'I am pure from evil, protected from the strife of those who are in their days.'
'You are not among them.
To whom, then, shall I report you?'
'You shall report me to the one whose ceiling is of fire, whose walls are living uraei, and the floor of whose house is in the flood.'
'Who is he?'
'It is Osiris.'
'Proceed, then.
See, you are reported.'

To be done in accordance with what happens in this hall of the Two Truths: [one who is] pure and clean, dressed in new clothing, shod in white sandals, his eyes painted with green eye-paint and black eye-paint, anointed with the finest myrrh, having offered bread, beer, cattle, fowl, incense on the fire, herbs and offerings.
Now, you shall make this picture on ground that is clean, done in yellow ochre and overlaid with field soil on which no pigs have trodden.
As for the one who makes this book for himself, he will flourish,
and his children will flourish with him.
He will be in the confidence of the king and of his courtiers.
There will be given to him a *šns*-loaf, a great *ds*-jug and meat on the altar of the great god.
He will not be turned back at any gate of the West.
He will be ushered in with the kings of Upper and Lower Egypt.
He will be in the following of Osiris. Truly correct, a million times.

It is a mystery of the Duat, a secret initiation of the necropolis, found in the great palace of the Mansion of the Great One in the time of the majesty of the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Semti(?), justified, as something found in the cavern of the mountain, as that which Horus made for his father Osiris-Wennefer, living forever.
